feedback.goal: Finalize the runtime-generation/HMR stacked integration after security review, preserving fail-closed approval, admission, attribution, and rollback behavior.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The HMR feature is directly based on the runtime-generation attestation commit and preserves its persisted and controller contracts.
Runtime and candidate identities bind once at session creation; candidate checkpoints are ineligible and final eligibility requires one unchanged admitted generation.
Candidate application cannot select a workspace package script; external launcher files are startup-digested and rechecked before and after approval verification before live writes.
Unrelated, unreadable, or digest-mismatched successful reloads reject pending admission and require confirmed baseline restoration.
DAL-024/ADR-0005 and DAL-025/ADR-0006 remain distinct, all capsules validate, focused and real-HMR proofs pass, and the complete repository gate passes.

outcome.summary: The stacked HMR feature preserves runtime-generation attestation, isolates approval verification from candidate scripts, aborts nonmatching admission, records final-only candidate eligibility, and passes final focused, real-HMR, repository, capsule, and review gates.

what_worked: Independent runtime and candidate inputs allowed one creation-bound recorder path without conflating their identities.
Operation-time launcher digest checks closed the workspace-script substitution seam before any candidate bytes are written.
Immediate rejection of nonmatching successful reloads made the documented fail-closed admission rule executable.
Focused negative tests and the real pinned composition probe exercised both synthetic failure paths and the actual Loader/HMR path.
what_failed: The first review found workspace-relative approval-command resolution and delayed rejection of unrelated reloads.
A second review found that launcher digests needed a post-verification check and that configured-entry digest mismatch lacked regression coverage.
The earlier combined-stack feedback record predates those fixes and is superseded by this record.

failures_and_inefficiencies.summary: The approval subprocess trust boundary was hardened only after the first complete gate, requiring two additional focused and repository-wide verification rounds.
failures_and_inefficiencies.suggested_action: Threat-review every operation-owned subprocess and event-admission state machine before the first full feature gate.

failures_and_inefficiencies.summary: Sibling feature branches independently selected the same requirement and ADR identifiers and competing recorder constructor seams.
failures_and_inefficiencies.suggested_action: Reserve requirement and ADR identifiers before parallel contract-bearing feature work.

evidence.summary: The committed review hardening sits on the rebased HMR feature and runtime-generation attestation parent.
DAL-024 owns runtime attestation and DAL-025 owns HMR candidate admission, attribution, rollback, and its non-authorizing evidence boundary.
The coordinator pins external launcher files, rejects drift around verification, and aborts pending activation on every nonmatching successful reload.
The recorder binds both optional generation sources once and derives independent runtime stability and final-only candidate eligibility.
Six focused suites passed 55 tests with one opt-in composition skip, including verifier isolation, launcher drift, reload mismatch, rollback, and dual-generation recording.
Three selected suites passed all 38 tests including the pinned local Loader/HMR admission and rollback composition case.
All three versioned capsules validated against the final hardened contract sources.
Typecheck, build, 34 test files with 219 passing tests and 7 opt-in skips, capsule validation, policy verification, core evaluation, and benchmark evaluation all passed without a hard stop.
The final focused review reported no findings; the only residual is the documented non-authorizing nature of HMR recorder attribution.

uncertainty.statement: HMR recorder attribution has no independently persisted admission receipt and therefore is not an authorization source.
uncertainty.resolution: Add a separately designed receipt and verifier only when a future automated consumer needs authenticated HMR admission evidence.

uncertainty.statement: No shared-profile mount, production candidate application, authoritative DSH runtime-generation producer, or awaited final-disposal boundary was exercised.
uncertainty.resolution: Keep these as separately approved upstream or deployment proofs.
